items.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described last week’s widespread Outlook outage as a “perfect storm” caused by a previously undetected software
items.content_excerpt: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described last week’s widespread Outlook outage as a “perfect storm” caused by a previously undetected software bug triggered by a specific pattern of network traffic. He acknowledged that better testing and safeguards could have prevented the disruption, which affected corporate communications worldwide. Nadella also warned that faster AI-driven software updates and security patches can create instability in legacy infrastructure. Separately, he highlighted Microsoft’s Copilot overhaul, which consolidates its AI tools into a single application, introduces usage-based pricing and allows customers to switch between models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Microsoft. The strategy aims to protect its enterprise software business as AI challenges traditional per-user licensing models. Azure revenue surged 48% to $33.2 billion in the latest quarter, driven by strong AI infrastructure demand. $MSFT

items.title: @MissionImpossibl “Neither paid cash.” - $AMZN put in $8B of cash in tranches across 2023–2024, and $GOOG put in several billion of its own.
items.content_excerpt: @MissionImpossibl “Neither paid cash.” - $AMZN put in $8B of cash in tranches across 2023–2024, and $GOOG put in several billion of its own. The fair criticism is that a lot of that money comes back as cloud spend on AWS and GCP. So “circular” is a reasonable word for it, but “free compute instead of cash” isn’t what happened. The amount of ANT compute committed to is far larger than either $GOOG or $AMZN cash. “The only guy who invested $500M cash.” - Plenty of investors paid cash, including Spark, Menlo, Lightspeed, Salesforce and sovereign funds. SBF’s ~$500M came from FTX, which was effectively customer money. The FTX bankruptcy estate sold that stake in 2024 for about $1.3B, so FTX’s creditors got roughly 2.5x. “Owns nothing now” is true of SBF, but because of the fraud case, not because the investment went bad.

items.title: $SLS The raise mainly tells us no deal is imminent, since you can't legally sell new shares while sitting on advanced M&A talks. But
items.content_excerpt: $SLS The raise mainly tells us no deal is imminent, since you can't legally sell new shares while sitting on advanced M&A talks. But "not now" isn't "never." With ~$285M in cash after the raise, SELLAS doesn't have to sell cheap. Buyers also usually wait for the full data and FDA alignment on the BLA, both expected in 1H 2027. The ~6% dilution barely matters to an acquirer because the cash comes with it. And $13 was a deal price, not a valuation: a 28% discount is normal when $150M is placed overnight after a 150%+ move. Add a rare positive Phase 3 OS result in AML (HR 0.59, mOS 24.0 vs 14.7 months) and J.P. Morgan/TD Cowen bringing in long-term institutions, and a 2027 buyout is still very much on the table. Buyout is unlikely near term but possible in 2027.

items.title: $CAPR Part 2 Inspectional Items (The July 2026 Form 483) For procedural items—specifically the single Form 483 observation from Capricor&#39
items.content_excerpt: $CAPR Part 2 Inspectional Items (The July 2026 Form 483) For procedural items—specifically the single Form 483 observation from Capricor's July 2026 Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) inspection—the rules are stricter: • Cannot be deferred if data integrity is in doubt: According to FDA BIMO inspection standards, the FDA will not approve a drug if an unresolved inspection finding casts doubt on the reliability of the clinical trial data or manufacturing safety. • Can be cleared via written response before approval: Capricor stated in its Q3 2026 regulatory update that the single observation involved administrative procedures, vendor oversight, and audit timeliness rather than data integrity, and that it has already submitted its formal corrective response. When a Form 483 is minor and procedural, the FDA routinely accepts the company's written corrective action plan and closes the item out concurrently with an approval decision—without needing a re-inspection.

items.title: $CAPR the FDA can approve a Biologics License Application (BLA) with open administrative or clinical questions—provided those items do not c
items.content_excerpt: $CAPR the FDA can approve a Biologics License Application (BLA) with open administrative or clinical questions—provided those items do not compromise patient safety, product manufacturing quality, or clinical data integrity. In Capricor’s case, how the FDA handles open items depends on whether they are scientific/clinical questions or inspectional/procedural observations: Part 1. Clinical & Efficacy If the FDA determines that the HOPE-3 trial proves Deramiocel helps upper-limb function, it does not need every long-term or secondary question answered before approval. Instead, the agency routinely uses two mechanisms: • As noted in FDA postmarketing reporting guidelines, the FDA can grant approval while legally requiring the sponsor to complete additional follow-up studies after launch—such as continuing long-term durability tracking or gathering further cardiac data. • The FDA can restrict the official prescribing label strictly to the proven population.

items.title: Gold fell about 3% at midday Wednesday, to its lowest since September 2025, and copper fell too. But gold miners ($GDX) fell about twice as
items.content_excerpt: Gold fell about 3% at midday Wednesday, to its lowest since September 2025, and copper fell too. But gold miners ($GDX) fell about twice as much as gold. Why? The short answer: some mining expenses change little in the short term, so falling prices squeeze earnings more sharply. That explains why miners are more sensitive, though it doesn't establish the cause of the day's exact moves. What moved the metals, per reports: traders betting the Fed will keep raising rates (gold), and a firm dollar plus doubts about AI data-centre spending (copper), InvestorsHub and Reuters reported. We found no company-specific catalyst for the miners. Full story: https://whymystockmoved.com/market/2026-11-18-why-gold-and-copper-stocks-are-down/

items.content_excerpt: $UNH fell 10.21% on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, closing at $349.91, after closing at $389.68 on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Health insurers sold off after CMS (the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the federal agency that runs Medicare) proposed a rule nicknamed CRUSH that would take problems found in a sample of audited Medicare Advantage charts and apply them to a plan's wider payments. Medicare Advantage is the version of Medicare run by private insurers, paid by the government per member. If the rule takes effect, insurers could owe the government larger repayments. Nothing is final yet. Moves like that make people ask one thing: where does the price sit against what the business is worth? items.content_excerpt: $UNH fell 10.21% on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, closing at $349.91, after closing at $389.68 on Tuesday, November 17, 2026. Health insurers sold off after CMS (the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the federal agency that runs Medicare) proposed a rule nicknamed CRUSH that would take problems found in a sample of audited Medicare Advantage charts and apply them to a plan's wider payments. Medicare Advantage is the version of Medicare run by private insurers, paid by the government per member. If the rule takes effect, insurers could owe the government larger repayments. Nothing is final yet. Moves like that make people ask one thing: where does the price sit against what the business is worth? items.title: General Motors is beginning preparations for CEO Mary Barra’s eventual succession, hiring an executive search firm to identify potential ext
items.content_excerpt: General Motors is beginning preparations for CEO Mary Barra’s eventual succession, hiring an executive search firm to identify potential external candidates while also evaluating a strong pool of internal executives, according to The Wall Street Journal. Barra, who has led GM since 2014, has reportedly been quietly preparing for an orderly leadership transition over the past several months. Her more than decade-long tenure makes her the second-longest-serving CEO in the automaker’s history and the first woman to lead a major global automaker. Her time in the role is roughly twice the average tenure of a modern S&P 500 CEO. Investors have reacted relatively calmly to the succession planning. GM shares initially slipped following the report but later recovered, trading around 0.6% higher, suggesting market confidence in the company’s deliberate approach to selecting its next leader. $GM $SPX

$CAPR Part 2 Inspectional Items (The July 2026 Form 483) For procedural items—specifically the single Form 483 observation from Capricor's July 2026 Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO) inspection—the rules are stricter: • Cannot be deferred if data integrity is in doubt: According to FDA BIMO inspection standards, the FDA will not approve a drug if an unresolved inspection finding casts doubt on the reliability of the clinical trial data or manufacturing safety. • Can be cleared via written response before approval: Capricor stated in its Q3 2026 regulatory update that the single observation involved administrative procedures, vendor oversight, and audit timeliness rather than data integrity, and that it has already submitted its formal corrective response. When a Form 483 is minor and procedural, the FDA routinely accepts the company's written corrective action plan and closes the item out concurrently with an approval decision—without needing a re-inspection.

$CAPR the FDA can approve a Biologics License Application (BLA) with open administrative or clinical questions—provided those items do not compromise patient safety, product manufacturing quality, or clinical data integrity. In Capricor’s case, how the FDA handles open items depends on whether they are scientific/clinical questions or inspectional/procedural observations: Part 1. Clinical & Efficacy If the FDA determines that the HOPE-3 trial proves Deramiocel helps upper-limb function, it does not need every long-term or secondary question answered before approval. Instead, the agency routinely uses two mechanisms: • As noted in FDA postmarketing reporting guidelines, the FDA can grant approval while legally requiring the sponsor to complete additional follow-up studies after launch—such as continuing long-term durability tracking or gathering further cardiac data. • The FDA can restrict the official prescribing label strictly to the proven population.
